# Licensing & Availability

## Release Timeline

ZTWIM reached general availability on January 23, 2026 [2]. The technology
preview was launched on May 19, 2025, approximately 8 months before GA [35].

## Bundling and Distribution

ZTWIM is bundled with Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (RHACM), Red Hat
Advanced Cluster Security (RHACS), and OpenShift Platform Plus [1]. It is not
available as a standalone product [1].

OpenShift Platform Plus components are inseparable — purchasing the bundle
includes all components regardless of which are deployed. The full Platform Plus
suite includes OpenShift Container Platform, Advanced Cluster Security, Advanced
Cluster Management, ODF Essentials, Quay, and Lightspeed.

No public pricing is available; organizations must contact Red Hat for quotes.

## Upstream Relationship

ZTWIM is built on upstream SPIRE, which is a CNCF graduated project [2]. Red Hat
extends the upstream with multicluster federation management, BYODB PostgreSQL
support, and flexible configuration through the operator model [2].

Deploying upstream SPIRE directly on OpenShift via Helm charts is explicitly not
a supported Red Hat product [38].

## Gaps and Limitations

1. OpenShift pricing for modest deployments ranges from approximately 12,000 to
   30,000 EUR per year, with a 20-40% premium for managed services. ZTWIM adds
   no incremental cost for Platform Plus subscribers but is inaccessible to
   organizations running base OpenShift.
2. Upstream SPIRE is production-viable without Red Hat's operator, as
   demonstrated by Indeed, Uber, and Macquarie Bank deployments [9][6][27].
3. The bundling model means organizations wanting only workload identity must
   purchase the full Platform Plus suite.
